title: Vegan Granola
subtitle: Golden oats and seeds sweetened with agave and coconut oil
excerpt: Vegan granola uses coconut oil and agave syrup in place of butter and honey, and the result is indistinguishable from the dairy version in terms of crunch and flavour, possibly better, since coconut oil gives a cleaner toast. This one leans heavily on the seeds for texture and keeps the nut content light. A batch lasts three weeks in the jar.
sourceNotes: A plant-based adaptation of classic baked granola, using agave syrup, derived from the agave plant, and coconut oil. Both ingredients became widely available in UK supermarkets through the 2010s alongside the growth of vegan cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in a sealed bag for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Keeps in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Granola stores well, make a large batch and keep in a jar.

content.text: Vegan granola works on the same principle as any other baked granola: coat the {{jumbo-oats}} oats and seeds in fat and sweetener, spread thin on a tray, and bake low and slow until deeply golden. {{coconut-oil}} Coconut oil is neutral in flavour once refined, so it gives a clean, even toast without the dairy note of butter. {{agave-syrup}} Agave syrup is thinner than honey, which helps it coat the dry ingredients more evenly and caramelise as it bakes. The {{sesame-seeds}} sesame seeds are what makes this version distinctive. They are small and nutty, and they toast faster than everything else, bringing a toasted note to the whole batch.

items.prepNote: use certified gluten-free oats if required

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 °C fan. Line a large baking tray with baking parchment.

Put the {{jumbo-oats}} jumbo oats, {{almonds}} almonds, {{sunflower-seeds}} sunflower seeds, {{pumpkin-seeds}} pumpkin seeds, {{sesame-seeds}} sesame seeds, {{cinnamon-ground}} cinnamon, and {{sea-salt-flakes}} sea salt into a large bowl. Stir to combine. Melt the {{coconut-oil}} coconut oil gently in a small pan or microwave until liquid but not hot. Stir in the {{agave-syrup}} agave syrup and {{vanilla-extract}} vanilla extract. Pour the wet mixture over the dry ingredients and mix until every oat is coated.

Spread the mixture across the lined tray in an even layer. Press it down firmly. A compact layer clusters better. Bake for 28 to 32 minutes, checking at the 25-minute mark. The granola should be deep golden at the edges and starting to colour in the middle. It will look slightly underdone when hot. It crisps as it cools.

Remove from the oven and leave on the tray, completely undisturbed, until entirely cold, at least 45 minutes. The agave sets as it cools and cements the clusters. Breaking into it while warm destroys them before they've had a chance to set. Once cold, break into pieces by hand and store in an airtight jar.
Sesame seeds burning before the oats are done: they're smaller and toast faster. Keep the temperature at 160 °C and check earlier than you think you need to.
Granola sticking to the parchment: the agave has caramelised onto the paper before the granola could cool and release cleanly. Use a fresh sheet of parchment next time.
Not sweet enough: agave is less sweet by volume than honey. Add another tablespoon if you prefer a sweeter granola.
Add 80 g of desiccated coconut to the dry mix before coating, it toasts golden and adds a tropical note that works well with mango and plant-based yoghurt.
Swap agave for maple syrup for a slightly more complex, less neutral sweetness.
Stir in 60 g of raisins or dried cranberries once the granola is completely cool. Don't add dried fruit before baking; it becomes rock-hard in the oven.
